title: All About a Spiky Animal
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about hedgehogs (the word "hedgehog" is not yet decodable: the "dge" spelling is not taught in this programme).
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about hedgehogs (the word "hedgehog" is not yet decodable: the "dge" spelling is not taught in this programme).

pages.text: The wind feels cold in the garden.
pages.illustration: A garden with bare branches and fallen leaves, a chilly autumn feel to the light.

pages.text: Moss spots a spiky animal in the leaf pile.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog peering through a pile of fallen leaves, spotting a wild hedgehog settling in.

pages.text: A spiky animal has sharp spikes on its back.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the wild hedgehog’s back, covered in rows of sharp brown spikes.

pages.text: A spiky animal eats a big snack to get set for the cold.
pages.illustration: The wild hedgehog munching on a beetle, building up its food store before the cold months.

pages.text: When it gets cold, a spiky animal looks for a snug spot.
pages.illustration: The hedgehog nudging its way into a thick pile of dry leaves and twigs.

pages.text: A spiky animal can curl into a tight ball.
pages.illustration: The hedgehog curled up completely into a tight, spiky ball shape.

pages.text: A spiky animal sleeps a long sleep in winter.
pages.illustration: The curled-up hedgehog resting still and quiet, tucked deep inside the leaf pile.

pages.text: A spiky animal can sleep for months on end.
pages.illustration: A snowy garden scene outside, with the hedgehog still snug and hidden under its leaf pile.

pages.text: In spring, a spiky animal wakes up.
pages.illustration: The hedgehog uncurling and stretching, waking up as spring sunlight warms the garden.

pages.text: Moss is glad the spiky animal is awake again.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog and the wild hedgehog standing together in the bright spring garden.
